clue.text: I carefully observe trouble — not good, putting it tersely

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is Latin for 'note well'

indicators.note: 'not good' asks for the letter standing for good to be dropped from the word before

parts.note: grief means trouble or distress

explanation.surface: Someone confesses, briefly, that they keep a careful eye on trouble that isn't good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes G away from GRIEF, leaving RIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something in brief is to say it concisely, which is putting it tersely.

clue.text: Is and isn't wrong to demand

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insists on deciding what is and isn't wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand something firmly and refuse to give way.

clue.text: Additions to window over sink? Not something I can comment on perhaps

definitions.text: Not something I can comment on perhaps

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece sits over the other

parts.note: blinds are fitted to windows
to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it

explanation.surface: Someone declines to talk about the new blinds fitted above the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: One cannot comment on what one cannot see.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind spot is an area someone cannot see, or a subject they know nothing about.

clue.text: Artless individual in group giving off singular energy

indicators.note: giving off one thing and taking another replaces the letter for singular with the letter for energy

parts.note: a genus is a group in biological classification
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A naive member of a group is giving off a unique kind of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving off' swaps the S of GENUS for E.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingénue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stage role.

clue.text: Father getting a garbled signal in contrived language

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

indicators.note: garbled means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest receives a muddled message in some made-up tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Franglais is French heavily mixed with English words, a hybrid jargon.

clue.text: I'm getting stuck into beer vessel without end

indicators.note: being stuck into something means being lodged inside it, so the first piece goes inside the others

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
I'm with the apostrophe dropped
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: Someone is getting into a beer barrel that seems to go on for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aimless has no goal or purpose, an 'end' in the sense of an aim.

clue.text: Poet: study area University put foremost

indicators.note: putting these at the front places them before the word for study

parts.note: a den is a study or private room

explanation.surface: A poet studies, with the university's area given top priority.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the 20th century.

clue.text: Unpleasant experience, accommodating gloomy playwright

indicators.note: accommodating means taking in, so the word for gloomy goes inside

parts.note: a mare, short for nightmare, is informal for an awful experience
low means gloomy or depressed

explanation.surface: A dreadful ordeal, put up with by a downcast dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan dramatist, author of Doctor Faustus.

clue.text: Ruminant, note, observed in climbing valley

indicators.note: something observed in a place is found within it, so the note goes inside
in a down answer climbing means going upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: A grazing animal is noted ascending a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns DALE into ELAD, and 'observed in' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope, which chews the cud.

clue.text: County cricket season reportedly prepared

indicators.note: as reported in speech, so the word is used for its sound

parts.note: cricket in Britain is played in summer
set means prepared, ready

explanation.surface: A county cricket team gets ready for the season.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in south-west England, pronounced like 'summer set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is an English shire in the south-west, and so a county.

clue.text: Protection from hackers initially going in hard with us, possibly

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters could be arranged another way, a cue to rearrange them
'initially' takes only the opening letter of the word going

explanation.surface: Computer security that goes in hard on our behalf against hackers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests computer hackers; in football a hacker kicks opponents' shins. 'possibly' rearranges G plus INHARDUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A shin guard is padding worn by footballers to shield the lower leg from kicks.

clue.text: Cultivate source of munitions — and do so again?

parts.note: to rear crops or animals is to raise or cultivate them

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone growing a supply of weapons wonders whether to repeat the exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do so' refers back to supplying munitions, so the definition is to arm once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to equip with weapons a second time, repeating the act of arming.

clue.text: Backed America and much of European country

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters for America are reversed

parts.note: US is the United States of America

indicators.note: much of a word but not all of it, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: Someone supported America and most of a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudan is a nation in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Rev might, after inviting duke in for tea

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it

indicators.note: inviting someone in means taking them inside, so the letter for duke goes inside

parts.note: power means might or strength

explanation.surface: A vicar, perhaps, after inviting a duke in for afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rev' looks like a vicar but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder is a Chinese green tea whose leaves are rolled into small pellets.

clue.text: Artist reversed cut in representation of harp — the best

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other
a representation of a word, here a rearranged version of its letters
turned back to front, so the letters for cut are read backwards

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
the elite are the best of a group

explanation.surface: An artist cut back the drawing of a harp, one of his finest works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation of' scrambles harp into PRHA, which 'in' opens to take the reversed cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pre-Raphaelite was a member of the 19th-century Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood of painters.

clue.text: Girl is after varying rough indicator of time

indicators.note: the girl comes after the rearranged letters
varying means changing, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl is guided by a rough sense of what time it is.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass measures time by sand running between two glass bulbs.

clue.text: One percent, upset with temperature, head off

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: One percent, upset by a fever, set off at the head of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercept is to stop or catch something on its way, to head it off.

clue.text: A little boy swallowing an insect

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the insect goes inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
a midge is a small insect

explanation.surface: A small boy gulps down a fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a tiny amount of something, a little bit.

clue.text: Late learner falls due to disapproving word about private office

parts.note: an investment or policy matures when it falls due for payment

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: tut is the word said in disapproval
a den is a private study or office

explanation.surface: A payment falls due owing to a disapproving remark about someone's private office.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature student is an adult who begins higher education later in life than usual.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink consumed by Voltaire à la légère

indicators.note: being consumed by these words means sitting inside them, so the answer is found within the run of letters

explanation.surface: Voltaire drinks something light-heartedly, as the French phrase puts it.
explanation.walkthrough: Accents are ignored. Real ale is a British term for traditionally brewed cask beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is cask-conditioned beer, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Sculptor records note with it

parts.note: EPs are extended-play records
te is a note in tonic sol-fa
in means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A sculptor keeps a record of a note and the work it goes with.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Epstein was a British-American sculptor of the 20th century.

clue.text: Article extracted from speeches satisfied rising organisation

indicators.note: taken out of, so the article is removed from the word for speeches

parts.note: one's says are one's spoken turns or speeches
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means going upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: met as in met a need, satisfied it

explanation.surface: An article extracted from speeches pleased a growing organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracted from' drops A from SAYS, leaving SYS; 'rising' turns MET into TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an ordered arrangement, an organisation of parts.

clue.text: Plane guided back, mark, after securing victory

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
read back, so the letters for guided are reversed

parts.note: led means guided

indicators.note: securing means holding in, so the word for victory goes inside

parts.note: a tag is a label or mark
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A plane is steered home and marked after making sure of a win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plane' is the aircraft, not the tool or a flat surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A delta wing is a triangular wing, and by extension an aircraft built with one.

clue.text: Soporific plant: scoundrel, out of Ecstasy, will import tons

indicators.note: importing brings something in, so the letter for tons goes inside
out of here means without, so the drug's letter is dropped

parts.note: a louse is a contemptible person
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A scoundrel who has run out of drugs will smuggle in tons of a sleep-inducing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops E from LOUSE, leaving LOUS; 'will import' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, eating the lotus fruit induced a dreamy forgetfulness, so it is a sleep-bringing plant.

clue.text: Contribution from one head assuming power

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the letter for power goes inside

parts.note: nut is slang for the head

explanation.surface: A leader who has taken power makes a contribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what one puts into a discussion or project, one's contribution.

clue.text: Right to block postponement? Get lost

indicators.note: to block something is to get in its way, so the letter for right sits inside the other word

parts.note: a stay of execution is a postponement

explanation.surface: A judge has the right to block a delay, and tells the appellant to go away.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander off course, which is to get lost.

clue.text: Time to follow Times, in time producing a special edition

indicators.note: one piece goes in another

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: this piece comes after the other

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, 'times'

explanation.surface: The Times newspaper rushes out a special edition just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' suggests the newspaper but is the multiplication sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional issue of a newspaper printed for breaking news.

clue.text: A lot of freedom to fix position

indicators.note: a lot of something but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: play is freedom of movement, as in a rope
to cement is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: Someone with plenty of liberty decides where to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement is the act of putting something in a particular spot, or that spot.

clue.text: Recalled article: trail is just starting

indicators.note: called back, so the letters of the article are read in reverse

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a scent is the trail an animal leaves

explanation.surface: An item withdrawn from sale, while the investigation's trail is only beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is newly come into being and beginning to develop.

clue.text: Insect seen round about, invading the whole room

indicators.note: an invader gets inside, so this piece goes within the word for the whole

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount

indicators.note: round means going around, so the insect's letters surround the abbreviation for about

parts.note: an ant is an insect
C, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: An insect is spotted crawling about and taking over the entire room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is only a link; the nested insertions give ANCT inside the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanctum is a private room where someone can retreat undisturbed.
